title: SPIFFE Workload API & OpenBao Policy Hardening Fixes

findings_addressed.title: signalloom-cardvault-agent and signalloom-fe-signalloom JWT roles issued 768h (32-day) tokens instead of the mission's 5-minute hard cap
findings_addressed.fix: Added token_ttl=5m, token_max_ttl=5m, token_type=batch to both roles.

live_verification.dynamic_login_result: bao write auth/jwt/login role=signalloom-cardvault-agent jwt=<real SVID> -> token_duration=5m (was 768h)

findings_addressed.title: signalloom-agent-generic role's bound_claims glob never matched a real SPIFFE sub because bound_claims_type defaulted to "string"
findings_addressed.fix: Added bound_claims_type=glob to the role write.

live_verification.dynamic_login_result: bao write auth/jwt/login role=signalloom-agent-generic jwt=<real agent-cardvault SVID, aud=openbao-supercredential> -> login succeeded (was: 400 claim "sub" does not match any associated bound claim values)

findings_discovered_this_card.severity: MEDIUM (fails closed -- correctness/availability defect, not an active bypass)
findings_discovered_this_card.title: signalloom-agent-templated's identity-templated KV policy path is unreachable by anyone, including the legitimate agent, for reasons independent of F2
findings_discovered_this_card.discovered_via: Live positive-control KV read attempted against signalloom-agent-generic's post-F2-fix issued token, going one step beyond the Required Tests to confirm the templated policy this card's fix was meant to finally unlock actually grants read access.
root_causes: auth/jwt is a single shared mount across signalloom-cardvault-agent, signalloom-fe-signalloom, signalloom-agent-generic, and agent-trust-*; OpenBao keys an identity-entity alias by (mount_accessor, sub-claim-value), so the same SPIFFE identity logging in via different roles on that mount shares one alias record whose metadata is overwritten (not merged) by whichever role logged in most recently.
Only signalloom-agent-generic declares claim_mappings {sub: sub}; every other role sharing the mount does not, so a login via any other role for the same identity clobbers alias.metadata.sub.

The raw sub claim is a full spiffe:// URI; its // is collapsed by standard HTTP path normalization (reproduced against OpenBao's own bao CLI), so even a correctly-resolved template segment does not survive the request path unmangled.
findings_discovered_this_card.live_verification: kubectl exec against the real kind-osramp OpenBao: three templated-path shapes tried (de-prefixed guess, literal spiffe:// prefix, list-on-prefix) all returned 403 preflight capability check, including for the legitimate agent reading its own intended path.
findings_discovered_this_card.recommendation: Retire signalloom-agent-templated/signalloom-agent-generic in favour of per-agent roles matching scripts/kagent-credentials.sh's already-correct bound_subject + dedicated-policy pattern, or give each multi-role identity a role-scoped alias instead of a mount-scoped one. Not fixed here: requires a design decision, not a one-field surgical edit, and is not named in this card's Objective/Approach/Deliverables.
findings_discovered_this_card.recommended_phase: SLAAT-P2-GOV triage or a new Phase 3 finding

findings_deferred.reason: Delegation gap (risk-reader/investigator) is deliberately unreachable today: both identities are labelled agent-trust.signalloom.io/scaffold=true and scripts/agent-trust-local.sh asserts their egress to OpenBao is network-denied by design. Provisioning an OpenBao role they cannot reach would not close a real gap.

SPIRE agent insecure_bootstrap/skip_kubelet_verification are demo-appropriate per the P1-3 dossier's own framing ('before any non-local deployment'); flipping either on the shared live cluster risks SVID-issuance loss for every concurrent sibling card with no tested rollback.

agent-cardvault hostPath-vs-spiffe-csi-driver volume migration requires a live Deployment rollout on a cluster other sibling cards are actively using; deferred to keep this card's blast radius to declarative role/policy edits only.
Static root token is a pre-existing accepted demo convention per the P1-3 dossier; rotating it touches every bootstrap Job's BAO_TOKEN env and risks locking out live re-bootstraps.

probe_openbao_acls_wildcard_check.note: delegation-coverage records (6 gaps) unchanged by this card, matching findings_deferred
